findings.description: FXFV7-A4-P1 anchor and neighbour arms enter at the 16:00-NY instant of the clock's decision_date, but the P2 clocks file carries decision_date = the EVENT date. The 16:00-NY entry instant therefore precedes the reaction-window end w1 by 16.5-28.0 hours on ALL 833 GB+CA clocks (byte-verified exhaustively). r_W is computed from 1h bars in [w0, w1], so the conditioning sign includes up to ~28h of price movement that happens AFTER the position is opened; 139/551 anchor and 113/444 neighbour entries even precede the window START w0 (GB DAY windows begin next 00:00Z after the event). The frozen authorities all say the opposite: P0 census frozen_semantics funded_decision_rule = 'first 16:00-NY DST-correct decision instant >= W-end'; the P2 clocks file's own rule string repeats it; the proposal asserts 'the 1h reaction window W is CLOSED before the decision instant by the funding rule, so the conditioning feature is strictly available pre-decision'. The +7d sham control arm DOES implement the correct rule (recomputes the first 16:00-NY after the shifted w1 via _first_decision_after; 0/486 entries before w1) — the correct construction existed in the same module and was selectively not applied to the true arms, so anchor-vs-sham comparisons are invalid on both sides. The A6-P2 family (its own trigger/entry machinery, no clocks-file dependence) byte-verifies clean (1032/1032 entries at trigger+1 close, holds verified, 0 episode overlaps, folds 246/426/360 matching D2 exactly). Remediation: recompute the funded decision_date per clock (first 16:00-NY >= w1) in the runner (or the clocks authority), then re-derive D2 feasibility, the sanitized dryrun, the novelty schedule and its rho for A4-P1, and re-run the diagnostic twin smoke; a semantics change at this point also re-triggers P-3 control recomputation (the sham already implements the corrected semantics, which is why it showed different counts).

findings.description: S0 exit-boundary inconsistency between families: A4-P1 excludes decisions whose exit would land beyond S0 end (s0_exit_excluded counter, 0/12 observed); A6-P2 clamps the exit at the series end via min(ie+HOLD, len-1) so late fold-3 decisions can book exits on post-S0 bars (forward booking of an open position — not lookahead — but a different boundary convention than A4-P1 within the same cycle).
